Linguistics

Radboud University

← Back to search
About this programme

UCR currently cannot construct a sufficiently close programme for a meaningful curriculum comparison.

Radboud Linguistics investigates how languages are structured, acquired, processed and used. It connects language science with cognition, multilingual societies, health and technology, supported by statistics, corpus analysis, experiments and independent research.

UCR offers psycholinguistics, stylistic analysis, rhetoric and some text-based computing. These are useful connections, but the available courses do not build the sustained study of language structure and linguistic research at the centre of this degree. We therefore show Radboud’s curriculum without presenting a UCR programme as a sufficiently close alternative.

Academic year: 2026–2027

External pathway: Ordinary non-abroad Linguistics programme

The adopted annual framework totals 180 EC: 120 required, 30 in two fixed Faculty of Arts minors and 30 in broadening electives. Each minor is a complete approved 15 EC package. Free electives exclude courses from the student’s own programme or specialisation. The 10 EC thesis requires the preceding language-research sequence, registration and a signed supervision agreement. B3 professional development includes a team think tank and portfolio. First-year mentoring and the diagnostic RADAr-NL language assessment, and B2 mentoring, carry no credits. The usual first-year study-advice threshold is 45 EC. Current annual requirements do not guarantee future offerings.
